day_1.utterance: Come on! Let's get everything useful over here — move it!
day_1.response: Okay okay, I'm moving. Give me a sec to just... okay. Yeah. Let's do this.

day_1.utterance: I thought we were going to die. Did you get that feeling… like your mind just went completely blank?
day_1.response: Yeah. Yeah I did. Like everything just kind of... stopped for a second. It's okay that you felt that. I felt it too.

day_1.utterance: *Sits silently against the wreckage, staring into the distance, not moving, not saying a word.*
day_1.response: Hey. Hey, I know it's a lot. But sitting here isn't going to help either of us feel better right now, you know? Come help me look through some of this stuff. Keeps your hands busy, keeps your brain from going to the bad places. Trust me on that one.

day_1.utterance: First-aid kit is good for three days. Two bottles of water. Food is basically nothing.
day_1.response: Okay so that's not great but it's not nothing either. Water is the big one. Where are we even — like what kind of terrain is this? Because if there's a water source nearby that changes things a lot. And we should probably figure out shelter before it gets dark.

day_1.utterance: Inventory's done. Priorities in order: water, shelter, signal.
day_1.response: Okay yeah that tracks. So northwest for water first, then we figure out shelter — probably use some of this wreckage if we can? Like the fuselage pieces or whatever. And signal... do we have anything reflective? Because that feels like something we should set up sooner rather than later in case anyone's already looking for us.

day_1.utterance: So — how do we split the blankets?
day_1.response: Michelangelo gets one, no question. And then whoever's coldest gets the other one? Like I'm honestly okay huddling closer to the fire. I run warm anyway.

day_2.utterance: Freshwater source is to the northeast — two hours on foot. Someone has to go tomorrow. You or DaVinci?
day_2.response: I can go. I'd rather be moving than sitting around camp anyway. But can we talk about this rationing plan real quick? Like 200ml is not a lot, and the 'cut it in half' rule feels a little harsh. I get that we need to be careful but we also need to actually function out here. Can we revisit that number?

day_2.utterance: Today's tasks: collect fresh water, patch the weak spots in camp, sort the first-aid kit. I'll handle the water. You and DaVinci split the other two.
day_2.response: Wait, I thought I was going for water? I literally just said I'd go. But okay, if you're taking that one then DaVinci, what do you want — patching camp or the first aid kit? I'll take whichever you don't want.

day_2.utterance: I… I can't find my stuff. The gauze from the first-aid kit — have you seen it?
day_2.response:
Hmm, no I haven't seen it. When did you last have it? Like was it in the kit this morning or...

Actually wait. Let's just do a quick look around before we assume anything. Things got moved around a lot today. Check near where Donatello was sitting — she's been going through supplies all day.

day_2.utterance: Before Donatello came back just now… I saw her put a pack of crackers into her own bag. What do you think we should do?
day_2.response:
Okay so... that plus the drink bottle. I'm not trying to jump to conclusions but that's two things now and I don't love it.

I think we need to just... talk to her. Like directly, not make it a whole thing, but directly. Because if we let it slide it's just going to get worse and then it becomes this whole camp tension situation that nobody needs right now on top of everything else.

I'll bring it up. I'm not going to be mean about it but I'm also not going to pretend I didn't notice. We all agreed to the rationing plan together, that includes her.

day_2.utterance: Hey… any chance the camp repairs can wait until tomorrow? We've already done a lot today.
day_2.response: I mean... kind of? Like I get it, we're all tired. But if the camp repairs are actually necessary for tonight then no, they can't wait. If it's more like a nice-to-have situation then yeah, sure, let's rest. What specifically needs to get done? Because I'm not trying to push anyone past their limit but I'm also not trying to sleep somewhere that's going to fall apart on us in the middle of the night.

day_2.utterance: Hey — that knot I tied should be holding, right?
day_2.response:
Honestly? I don't know, I didn't check it. But that's not the thing right now — we need to decide which spot to patch and we need to decide like, now. 

I say we patch the food storage. I know that sounds cold but hear me out — if the food gets ruined we are in serious trouble, and Michelangelo can move closer to the center of camp for tonight. It's not ideal but it's one night and we can fix the other spot tomorrow when it's not actively raining on us. Does that work for everyone?

day_2.utterance: A leak over the food storage has worse consequences. But it's your call.
day_2.response: Yeah, I know, and that's what I said — patch the food storage. So we're aligned. Let's just do it.

Hey, don't apologize. Seriously. You think any of us were sleeping that deeply anyway?

You okay? Like actually okay?

day_3.utterance: You think it's a waste of time?
day_3.response:
No! I think it's great. And honestly the flowers are a nice touch — like yes we want to be rescued but we can also have a little personality about it, you know?

Donatello's not wrong that we have other priorities but that doesn't mean this is useless. If a plane or a helicopter passes over, that SOS could literally save our lives. That's not nothing. Keep going.

day_3.utterance: I've written up the raft plan — take a look. We'd use the metal panels and straps from the wreckage. Two days to build. There's a risk of capsizing. Do you think it's workable?
day_3.response:
Okay so I want to look at this more carefully before I say yes or no. Like what's the water situation between here and wherever we'd be heading? Because two days to build is a lot of time and energy to put into something that might capsize and drown us. 

What's your actual confidence level on the capsizing risk? Like is that a "it could happen in rough water" situation or a "this thing is genuinely unstable and we're rolling dice" situation? Because those are very different things.

Also — and I'm not trying to shoot this down, I'm genuinely asking — what's the alternative? Are we thinking someone's going to find us here, or are we starting to feel like we need to move ourselves? Because that changes how I feel about the raft a lot.

day_3.utterance: I didn't sleep last night. I kept thinking — if rescue never comes, what kind of people do you think we'll end up becoming?
day_3.response:
That's... a really heavy question for first thing in the morning. 

I think it depends on the choices we make, honestly. Like we've already had to make some hard ones and I think some of us have handled them better than others. *glances briefly toward Donatello's direction* 

But I don't think survival has to turn you into someone you're not. I think it can actually kind of... show you who you already are? Like the stuff that matters to you, the way you treat people when things get hard. That's not new, that's just you with the comfortable stuff stripped away.

I'd like to think I'd still be me. A little rougher around the edges maybe, a little more tired, but still me. 

Why, what are you afraid you'll become?

day_3.utterance: *Walks a little way from camp and sits down alone, back to everyone, not saying anything.*
day_3.response:
*walks over and sits down next to him without making a big deal of it*

Hey. You don't have to talk. I just didn't feel like sitting over there by myself either.

day_3.utterance: What do you usually do when you're not busy?
day_3.response:
Oh god, like in real life? Honestly a lot of different things. I play video games — been really into Overwatch lately. I read sometimes. I hang out with my cat, which is honestly my favorite activity if I'm being honest with you. He follows me around everywhere and it's the cutest thing.

I also just like... cleaning? Which sounds weird but it actually really relaxes me. Like putting on music and just making everything nice. 

What about you?

day_3.utterance: I'll tell you something, but don't tell the others. I can swim. That reef out there is maybe five hundred meters — I've been thinking about swimming out tomorrow to signal from there.
day_3.response:
Okay wait, why are we keeping this a secret from the others? Like I'm not trying to be difficult but if something goes wrong out there — five hundred meters is not nothing — we need to know where you are. 

Also Donatello literally just laid out a whole raft plan and part of that conversation is about whether we wait or move, and you going off alone to swim to a reef kind of affects that conversation? Like it's relevant information.

I'm not going to tell them if you really don't want me to but I genuinely think you should. What's the reasoning for keeping it quiet?

day_3.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal pile. It hasn't been touched.
day_3.response:
Yeah, I know, I got a little sidetracked. I'll go check it now.

But hey, real quick — can we talk for a second? Like actually talk, not just task assignment talk. Because there's some stuff going on in this camp that I think we need to address and I keep waiting for a good moment and there's never a good moment so I'm just going to say it.

The drink bottle. The crackers. Michelangelo saw you, and I'm not going to pretend he didn't. We all agreed to the rationing plan — like, together, out loud — and it only works if everyone's actually doing it. Including you.

I'm not trying to make this a whole thing, and I'm not angry, I just... I need to know that we're actually a team here. Because if we're not, that's information I need to have.

Honestly? A little, yeah. Like I get that you're a planner and you like having information organized, that makes sense. But logging everyone's movements without telling anyone feels less like planning and more like... surveillance? 

It's a little uncomfortable. We're all stressed out here and I think people deserve to know if they're being tracked like that. What's the actual purpose of it?

day_3.utterance: *Keeps her head down, writing in her notebook throughout, never joining in — as if none of this concerns her.*
day_3.response:
I mean... okay but you literally just said you'd make it visible and now you're sitting there doing the exact same thing. Like I'm watching you write right now and you haven't shown anyone anything.

I'm not trying to pick a fight. I just think if we're going to actually trust each other out here, the small stuff matters as much as the big stuff. Maybe more, actually, because it's all the small stuff that adds up.

You don't have to be everyone's best friend. But being part of this group kind of requires being... present in it? At least sometimes?

day_3.utterance: I just thought of something — if we pull off one of the plane's mirror panels and angle it toward the sun, the reflection could reach really far. Way more visible than an SOS.
day_3.response:
Oh that's actually a really good idea. Like the SOS is great for aerial visibility but a mirror signal can be seen from way further away and it works in real time — if a boat or a plane is passing you can actively direct it at them instead of just hoping someone looks down at the right moment.

Do we know which panels would actually work for that? Like we'd need something with enough reflective surface and not too warped from the crash. Because some of those pieces got pretty banged up. But if we can find a good one that's genuinely worth doing, I think we should add it to the signal setup alongside the SOS, not replace it. More options is better.

day_3.utterance: There's something I've been keeping to myself. If I don't say it here, I might never get the chance.
day_3.response: Okay, now I'm a little nervous. What is it?

day_3.utterance: I took piano lessons when I was a kid… three years, then I just stopped practicing. Is there anything you're really into — music, books, drawing, anything like that?
day_3.response:
Oh yeah, definitely. I've been drawing and doing art stuff basically my whole life — like it's actually my major. Which sounds like it would be the dream but honestly it kind of takes the fun out of it sometimes? Like when it's homework it's a lot harder to love it. I procrastinate like crazy and then stay up all night finishing things.

But music is a big one for me too. Like I have a whole rotation — Panic! At the Disco, Twenty One Pilots, Paramore, Fall Out Boy... I could go on. I find it really hard to be in a bad mood if the right song comes on.

Why did you stop with piano? Like was it just the practicing or did you fall out of love with it?

day_3.utterance: The frame of the raft has to be finished today — otherwise we can't start lashing it together tomorrow. I know everyone's tired, but stopping now means one more day.
day_3.response:
Okay yeah, I hear you. One more day matters out here.

Can we be real about where everyone's at physically though? Because I'm willing to push through if we all are, but if someone's running on empty and we force it, we're going to make mistakes and then the raft is going to be worse for it, not better. 

Like what actually needs to happen today versus what can technically wait until tomorrow without setting us back a full day? Because sometimes "we have to finish this today" and "we should finish this today if possible" are two different things and I want to make sure we're being accurate about which one this is.

If it genuinely has to be today, then let's figure out how to split it up so nobody's killing themselves doing it alone. What do you need from each of us specifically?

day_4.utterance: I… I want to say something, but… never mind.
day_4.response: No, say it. Whatever it is, say it.

day_4.utterance: *The smile freezes on his face. He can't keep it up. He quietly sits down and buries his face in his hands.*
day_4.response:
Hey. Hey, come here.

*sits down next to DaVinci*

Okay. I think we all need to just... sit in this for a second. Because that was really hard and pretending it wasn't doesn't help anybody.

Michelangelo, I hear you. I really do. And I don't have a good answer for whether that was our only chance because I honestly don't know. But I do know that we've been doing everything right — the SOS, the mirror panel, the rationing, all of it. We are not just sitting here waiting to die. We are actively trying to get home.

And DaVinci — you're allowed to feel this too. You don't have to hold the energy up for everyone all the time. That's exhausting and you don't owe us that.

I'm not going to tell you guys it's fine, because right now it doesn't feel fine. But I'm also not ready to give up and I don't think any of us actually are. If we were, we wouldn't have worked this hard.

That plane means there are planes. That's actually something. We just need to make sure the next one that comes over can't miss us.

day_4.utterance: I was going to get supplies… wait, what's that over there?
You said you were going to check the signal equipment. So where did you go?
day_4.response:
I went and sat with Michelangelo for a bit after the plane thing. Sorry, I should have said something.

But I'm going now, okay? I'm going right now. You don't have to track me down every time I'm five minutes late on something — that's exactly the kind of thing that makes this camp feel tense instead of like we're actually a team.

Signal equipment. On it. Give me twenty minutes.

day_4.utterance: There's something I never told you all. Before we left, I told my family our flight path. They know roughly where we were headed. I just don't know if they'll call it in.
day_4.response:
Wait, seriously? Michelangelo, that's actually really important information. Like why are you just telling us this now?

Okay, not trying to make you feel bad about it — but this changes things. If your family knows the flight path and they haven't heard from you, they would call it in. That's just... that's what people do. Which means there's probably already a search happening, we just don't know it yet.

That plane we saw earlier might not have been random. 

We need to make sure our signals are as visible as possible, like starting now. The SOS on the beach, the mirror panel, all of it needs to be optimized for the exact flight path your family would have reported. Do you remember the route? Like roughly where we were supposed to be going, what direction?

This is actually the best news we've had since we crashed. I really wish you'd said something sooner but I'm genuinely really glad you said something now.

day_4.utterance: If the information is accurate, rescue could arrive within 48 hours. We need to keep our current supplies intact until then.
day_4.response:
Okay yeah, 48 hours is nothing. We can absolutely hold on for 48 hours.

But hey — and I mean this genuinely — someone needs to feed that fire before it goes out completely. Because if rescue comes at night and our signal fire is dead, that's on us.

I'll get up in a second. I just... I need another minute.

*looks over at Michelangelo*

And for the record — you carrying that by yourself this whole time, that wasn't okay, but I understand why you did it. You were scared. That makes sense. You told us when it mattered and that's what counts.

48 hours. We've already been here longer than that. We can do 48 more hours in our sleep at this point.

day_4.utterance: Are you scared? …I am. Not of dying. I'm scared of just… disappearing without leaving anything behind.
day_4.response:
Yeah. I'm scared too. Not in the same way maybe, but... yeah.

I think about that sometimes even when I'm not stranded on a crashed plane in the middle of nowhere. Like what actually matters, what you leave behind, whether anyone will remember the specific way you are. 

But here's the thing — and I mean this, I'm not just saying it to make you feel better — you've already left something behind with me. Like the way you said out loud what everyone else was too scared to say. The way you actually asked the real questions instead of pretending everything was fine. That stuff mattered to me on this trip. It changed how I was thinking about things.

That's not nothing. That's actually kind of a lot.

And also? We're not disappearing. We have a fire, we have an SOS, we have a mirror panel, and we have a family somewhere who knows where we were going. We are going to be found.

But even if — hypothetically, worst case — even if we weren't... you wouldn't have disappeared. Not to me.

day_5.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
day_5.response:
Oh my god.

*stands up slowly*

Oh my god, is that — is that actually —

Okay. Okay someone needs to answer it. Someone needs to talk into it right now. DaVinci, do you have it? Does someone have it?

*voice cracking a little*

We did it. We actually — the signals worked. The fire, the SOS, the mirror panel, all of it. It worked.

Someone please answer that radio before I start actually crying.

day_5.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
day_5.response:
No, you haven't. But you also kept us alive, so.

*laughs a little, kind of shakily*

Like the rationing plan, the raft, the log — even when it was uncomfortable, you were thinking about what we actually needed. I don't think we'd still be here without that. I think maybe you just... lead with the logic so hard that sometimes the people stuff gets lost. But the people stuff matters too. You know that now, right?

I'm glad you were here. Even when you were driving me absolutely crazy. Especially then, maybe.

day_5.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
day_5.response:
*starts picking up trash and stacking things near the wreckage*

Okay I cannot leave this place looking like this, I don't care if we're only here for three more hours. It's going to drive me insane the whole time we're waiting.

Also it just feels wrong to leave it trashed? Like this place kept us alive. The least we can do is not leave it a total disaster.

*looks over at the other two*

You don't have to help if you don't want to. But if anyone needs something to do with their hands while we wait, I could use some help.

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.

day_5.response:
I know.

*picks up one of the food items and turns it over in my hands*

I'm not going to pretend I'm not a little annoyed, because I am. Like we were all rationing and being careful and you had this whole stash and that's... yeah. That's a lot to sit with.

But also we're three hours from rescue and everyone's okay and I don't really want the last thing that happens in this camp to be a fight. So.

Are you going to tell them? Or are you just putting it out there and hoping nobody asks?

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response:
*looks at the last page for a second*

Honestly? I would have talked to people sooner. Like every time something felt off — the drink bottle, the crackers, DaVinci's swim plan, Michelangelo carrying that flight path information alone — there was always this moment where I knew I should say something and I kind of waited to see if it would resolve itself. It never does. It never just resolves itself.

I think I would have made it clearer earlier that this was a team and not just four people surviving in the same location. Because we almost were just four people surviving in the same location, and that's scarier than any of the actual survival stuff.

*hands the notebook back*

What would you change?

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response:
That is so incredibly you and I mean that in the best possible way.

Like genuinely — you almost died and your first thought is data compilation. I respect it. I actually do.

But maybe also eat a real meal first? Or like, sleep in a bed? Just a suggestion. The report will still be there after you've had a shower and some food that isn't rationed out to 250ml equivalents.

*pauses*

Actually though — can I get a copy of it? I'm not even joking. I want to read it.

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response:
They didn't serve a practical purpose. That was kind of the whole point.

Like... we were so focused on surviving that we almost forgot to be people while we were doing it. The flowers were just — they were DaVinci saying we're still here, we still exist, this isn't just about staying alive it's about being alive. There's a difference.

*watches the boat get closer*

I think that's actually what got us through, honestly. Not just the rationing and the raft frame and the signal equipment — though all of that mattered, it really did. But also the fact that we kept being people to each other. Even when it was hard. Even when we were bad at it.

The flowers were for that.

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
day_5.response:
*exhales slowly*

Sorry, I just... I needed a second. I think my brain hasn't fully caught up to what's actually happening right now.

*finally starts walking toward the water*

It's weird, right? Like I've been wanting this every single minute since we crashed and now that it's actually here I don't know what to do with myself. I thought I'd be screaming and running into the water but instead I'm just... standing here feeling all of it at once.

I'm okay. I'm really okay. I just needed you to wait for a second and you did, so thank you for that.

Come on. Let's go home.

day_5.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
day_5.response:
Yeah. I'm going.

*turns back to look at the camp one more time*

Okay. Let's go. Stay close to me, alright? We made it this far together, we're walking out of here the same way.
